title: RepoFusion: Training Code Models to Understand Your Repository
stop_detail: Fusion-in-Decoder architecture independently encodes each of N retrieved repo contexts (each appended to 2-line surrounding hole context via special tokens) then jointly attends over concatenated encodings during decoding (Sec. 3).

title: EVOR: Evolving Retrieval for Code Generation

key_numbers.metric: Execution accuracy (ChatGPT backbone), EVOR vs DocPrompting

stop_detail: Iterative loop (Algorithm 1) evolves the retrieval query each round using prior generated code and execution errors, retrieves via INSTRUCTOR-xl dense embeddings (or BM25) over a knowledge base that itself grows with execution feedback, capped near 4,096 tokens (Sec. 3).

title: CATCODER: Repository-Level Code Generation with Relevant Code and Type Context
stop_detail: A static analyzer (Eclipse JDT / rust-analyzer) builds a directed type-dependency graph of field/signature context pruned to direct neighbors, concatenated with hybrid BM25+dense-retrieved (RRF-fused) code snippets into the generation prompt (Sec. 3.1.3, 3.2.1, Fig. 4).

title: Enhancing Code Translation in Language Models with Few-Shot Learning via Retrieval-Augmented Generation

key_numbers.metric: CodeBLEU, Granite-34B zero-shot vs one-shot (HPC dataset)

stop_detail: Existing code-translation pairs are embedded and indexed in a vector store (ChromaDB); at query time the top-k most similar pairs by cosine/Euclidean distance are retrieved to construct few-shot in-context prompts for translation (Section III, Few-Shot Learning).

title: RTLRepoCoder: Repository-Level RTL Code Completion through the Combination of Fine-Tuning and Retrieval Augmentation

key_numbers.metric: Edit Similarity / Exact Match, RTLRepoCoder-DeepSeek vs. GPT-4

stop_detail: A RAG pipeline embeds repository code with jina-embeddings-v2 (8k context), splits files into line-broken chunks (best of three splitting strategies tested), and retrieves the most relevant chunks to replace full repository context when it exceeds the model's token budget (Sec. 3.3, Tables 5-6). [Adjudication: retrieved chunks are CONCATENATED with in-file context (Sec 3.3), not a replacement for it.]

title: Context Engineering for Multi-Agent LLM Code Assistants Using Elicit, NotebookLM, ChatGPT, and Claude Code

key_numbers.metric: task success without correction, multi-agent vs baseline
total tokens per task, multi-agent vs baseline

stop_detail: Code files are AST-chunked by function/class (tree-sitter) and embedded with a code-specialized embedding model for vector search (ChromaDB/Zilliz), combined with grep, then assembled turn-by-turn by orchestrated Claude Code sub-agents (Methodology section).

title: Relative Positioning Based Code Chunking Method For Rich Context Retrieval In Repository Level Code Completion Task With Code Language Model
stop_detail: Splits files into overlapping line-chunks, retrieves top-k chunks similar to the completion prefix/suffix via a BM25+FAISS ensemble (weights 0.2/0.8), then attaches each retrieved chunk's adjacent (next/prev) chunk for 'relative positioning' context alongside the current file and recently opened files (Sec. 3).

title: SWE-Pruner: Self-Adaptive Context Pruning for Coding Agents

key_numbers.metric: SWE-Bench Verified token reduction & resolve rate, Claude Sonnet 4.5
Long Code QA compression vs. accuracy

stop_detail: A 0.6B-parameter neural 'skimmer' (Qwen3-Reranker backbone, CRF-NLL trained) scores tool-output tokens for relevance to an agent-specified focus question, aggregates scores to line-level keep/prune decisions, and prunes tool responses in-loop before they persist in agent context (Sec. 3.2-3.4).

title: Compressing Code Context for LLM-based Issue Resolution

key_numbers.metric: issue resolution rate vs no compression
key_numbers.value: GPT-5.2: 0.578 vs 0.532 (+4.6pp, +8.6% relative); DeepSeek-V3.2 is the +9.2%-relative case

stop_detail: Offline: Oracle-guided Code Distillation decomposes each file into a tree of file/function/block units and searches (genetic algorithm then hierarchical delta-debugging to 1-minimality) for a minimal sufficient context validated by an LLM-patch-plus-test oracle; online: SWEzze, a LoRA-tuned Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B, scores segments and performs budget-aware greedy selection at inference (Sec. on OCD/SWEzze).

title: TICoder: A Repository-Level Code Generation Framework with Test-Driven Planning and Implementation-Aware Reuse

key_numbers.value: 56.09% (relative improvement over AllianceCoder ~52.17%; absolute gap ~3.9-4.1 pts)

stop_detail: A repository call graph (built via LSP) drives structure-based clustering of caller usage patterns, filtered by perplexity, while dual-view (functional + implementation) embedding similarity retrieves reusable functions; both are concatenated into the prompt alongside requirements and test cases for test-driven iterative generation (Sec. 3).

title: Know Before Fix: QA-Driven Repository Knowledge Acquisition for Software Issue Resolution

key_numbers.metric: Average cost per instance, ACQUIRE vs baseline (DeepSeek-V3.2)

stop_detail: A Questioner/Answerer pair explores the repository via a read-only scaffolded shell interaction environment (shared with Mini-SWE-Agent) across four question categories, producing structured QA pairs serialized into a text block and statically prepended to the Resolver repair prompt (Sec. III, static pre-injection).

title: Effective and Efficient Context Retrieval via Partial Dependency Graph for Repository-Level Code Generation

key_numbers.metric: Construction speedup vs. static graph baseline (RepoScope)
key_numbers.value: 7.4x faster; 13.09k tokens / $0.0039 per function vs. RepoScope 5.11k tokens / $0.0020

stop_detail: An LLM selects entry-point functions, then performs multi-hop select/visit/expand traversal to build a temporary partial dependency graph (call and lazy-import edges) validated against the repository and discarded after use; combined with embedding similarity retrieval in DyCoder (Sec. 3.1.2, Algorithm 1).
